I like the article. And I fully agree on the remark that (in my words) science is not (and in my opinion should never be) settled. Whenever we learn or experience something new, existing science might need to be adapted.
This also holds for general knowledge. The older I get the more the feeling grows that there is so much I do not know. LLMs on the other hand seem to act contrary, everything seems a hard fact in the way it is told. And I think/seem to see that a lot of people put a lot of trust in these ‘facts’.
So the best option for me remains: keep an open mind and think for myself. Not always easy though to not get caught in existing believes and previous experiences.

text:
You have to know quite a bit about LLMs to do a good job - as with other powerful tools. And it would help a lot if we had more transparent LLMs, whose learning set could be scrutinized.

Perhaps the two biggest issues with LLMs, other than their huge negative externalities, are opacity and the exceptional ease for using them badly.

text: Hello! I came across this community mostly through Mastodon. I work as a web developer at an information design studio (lots of overlap in "how to see and do cool things through digital interfaces" there), but have also been working on a lot of personal projects around poetic programming and poetic web experiences since my undergrad days. My more ambitious and confusing (to myself) projects include an experiment in trying to design and develop a programming language with poetry in mind. I haven't formally studied much programming language theory so it goes over my own head, like some of the more technically complicated projects shared here. But I am really enamoured with the overall idea of "feeling of computing" and am very excited to be here and to learn more!

text: There are software developers using LLMs without even reading the code they produce, they just manually see if the app works. Are scientists doing this too with just testing some end product? I hope not. Seems like a different problem from software where it's more about the output than finding some novel new way to do things, atleast in app development.
